transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Peregrine HoML), Omar Singh (Peregrine Infra), Tara Miles (Peregrine Product)

--- Auto Summary / Quick notes (auto-gen may be fuzzy) ---
- Customer wants to validate unit economics for chat-assistant feature across ~3M monthly sessions; concerned about runway and latency.
- POC will run small dedicated benchmark; focus metrics: tokens/call, cache hit rate, batching factor, 95p latency, cost/session.
- Next: spreadsheet, 48hr bench, security docs, SOW.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick run-through of agenda — we want to nail the success criteria and the measurement plan for the POC, especially around cost per session and latency.
[00:23] Lena: thanks, yeah we have runway concerns. we need to project costs for the next 6 months if the feature scales. baseline is about 10k daily active sessions now, expecting 100k over 6 months.
[00:45] Omar: on infra side we prefer VPC peering for the POC if possible, for compliance reasons. also curious about dedicated vs hosted cost delta.
[01:05] Diego: great, we can do VPC peering in Redwood Private or a hosted integration with peered endpoints. cost-wise we typically show hosted per-token and then dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput — we'll layout both.
[01:30] Tara: high-level success: 95th pct latency under 350ms and cost per session < $0.02 — those are ballpark but we want that guardrail.
[01:45] Maya: perfect. can I confirm the expected tokens per session?
[02:00] Lena: typical session is multi-turn: ~60 tokens in prompt, ~120 tokens generated on average, so ~180 tokens roundtrip. some outliers go to 800 tokens.
[02:20] Diego: ok that's helpful. for modeling we split into avg and tail. also caching/prefix reuse can cut prompt tokens by up to 40% if you have reusable system prompts or long histories we can KV cache.
[02:45] Omar: pause — how do you quantify cache savings? what assumptions do you need from us?
[02:58] Diego: we ask for sample traffic or sample session traces; we compute prefix reuse % — e.g., 30% of sessions reuse the same user system prompt or SOP, which reduces tokens sent to model. in our spreadsheet we'll include conservative (10%), expected (25%), optimistic (50%) cache hit scenarios.
[03:25] Maya: and we'll show per-token nominal hosted price in the sheet; for illustration let's use something like $0.0007 per input token and $0.0012 per output token for the model class they'll test — those are example placeholders.
[03:45] Lena: that's in the ballpark. if we do dedicated reserved, how do you show committed vs burst economics?
[03:55] Diego: dedicated gives lower per-token GPU cost but you pay reserved capacity — we model amortized slots. for example, a dedicated 8xA100 pool amortized might lower per-token to $0.0004 output under steady utilization but you need to hit throughput targets to be economical. we'll include utilization sensitivity curves.
[04:20] Tara: can Redwood do quantized variants? we're exploring 8-bit and 4-bit to reduce cost.
[04:30] Diego: yes, runtime supports 8-bit/4-bit quantized model variants; quality regressions vary by model. we'll include a quality vs cost tradeoff table and recommend a set of prompts for regression testing.
[04:50] Omar: what's the suggested benchmark load shape? constant RPS or diurnal?
[04:58] Maya: for planning we usually run a 48-hour window with a mix: steady-state 50 RPS and a 5x burst window to test autoscaling and latency. you pick targets; we can mirror your realistic traffic shape if you provide traces.
[05:20] Lena: 50 RPS steady seems okay; peak maybe 250 RPS. our current infra can handle some of that but not the model cost.
[05:30] Diego: note: batching behavior is crucial. under higher RPS you can batch more, which lowers per-token compute cost but can increase latency. we'll model batching factor vs latency tradeoff.
[05:50] Tara: give an example of batching impact? numbers help the execs.
[05:58] Diego: sure, rough example: at 50 RPS with avg tokens 180, continuous batching with a target batch size of 16 reduces per-token cost by ~22% compared to batch size 1, with median added latency of ~30ms; at 250 RPS you can push batch sizes to 64 and gains become ~35-40% at the expense of 70-120ms extra median latency depending on KV cache behavior.
[06:30] Omar: does KV cache change batching?
[06:35] Diego: caching reduces sequence length and sometimes reduces async batching effectiveness because shorter sequences finish faster, but net compute cost is lower. caching + batching together often gives multiplicative wins.
[06:50] Maya: practical callouts — we'll ask for a sample 24-48 hour traffic sample and 50-100 representative prompts. Diego will run a synthetic replay to estimate realistic batch distributions and effective tokens/sec.
[07:10] Lena: we can extract a week of anonymized logs and strip PII. we'll need a quick template of what you need.
[07:20] Maya: I'll send a traffic-capture template after this call.
[07:30] Tara: on security — SOC2 docs and SAML/SCIM are must-haves for our procurement. do you provide customer-managed keys?
[07:40] Maya: yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM and for Hosted we offer BYOK integrations for enterprise. we'll attach SOC2, pen test summary, and network diagram.
[07:55] Omar: latency SLO under peering — any expected extra hop?
[08:05] Diego: with VPC peering you should see minimal extra RTT. the dominant component is model compute; network is usually <10ms additional if in same region.
[08:15] Lena: ok. Let's talk pass/fail criteria again. cost per session < $0.02 and 95p < 350ms. are those feasible?
[08:25] Diego: feasible but conditional — depends on cache hit and batching. our template scenarios: with 25% cache hit and batching factor 16 at 50 RPS we can model cost/subsession around $0.012-$0.018 given the example price points. tails may push higher.
[08:50] Maya: we'll surface three scenarios in the spreadsheet: conservative, expected, optimistic. we'll also show committed-dedicated break-even points.
[09:05] Tara: timeline: we want results before the end of March. what's realistic?
[09:15] Maya: 4-week POC: week1 integration and traffic handoff, week2 small-scale bench and smoke tests, week3 full 48-hour bench and tail testing, week4 analysis and decision. so if we start week of 2/23 we close by week of 3/22.
[09:35] Omar: what's needed from infra to start? VPC peering info, ephemeral keys, and sample traffic; also allow IP ranges for the test.
[09:45] Diego: we'll need a service account and minimal firewall/ACLs. Diego: (additional) if you prefer we can run everything in Redwood Private in your VPC to avoid egress.
[10:05] Lena: curious — for measurement, do you instrument token-level cost on your end?
[10:12] Diego: yes; Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns and per-route latency histograms. we'll provide a shared dashboard during bench window and export CSVs.
[10:25] Tara: for the exec deck we need a simple KPI slide: cost/session, latency 50/95/99, cache hit, batch factor, and projected monthly cost at growth scenarios.
[10:40] Maya: we'll produce that slide as part of the POC deliverables.
[10:50] Omar: any regulatory constraints around log retention we should be aware of?
[10:55] Maya: retention configurable; we can redact or not store request bodies in the hosted offering for the POC; Private you control retention.
[11:05] Lena: on the topic of model regression tests, how do we protect quality if we use quantized variants?
[11:12] Diego: we recommend prompt-focused A/B tests and a small eval set; we'll compute rouge/bertscore or domain-specific metrics and set a regression threshold (e.g., <1% drop in score). we'll include that as part of success criteria.
[11:30] Tara: awesome. any blockers you see?
[11:35] Diego: only getting the sample traces and VPC info in time. also need to lock the cost placeholders for the bench — we'll call them placeholders and then replace with actual model pricing once model chosen.
[11:50] Maya: agreed. we'll list model candidates in the spreadsheet.
[12:00] Lena: final question — do you have references doing similar POCs for retail or fintech?
[12:08] Maya: yes, we'll share one-pagers and anonymized case studies. will include a short note about the size and outcomes.
[12:20] Tara: ok let's summarize next steps.
[12:25] Maya: recap: Maya send spreadsheet + traffic template + SOC2/docs (due 2/12/26). Diego+Omar schedule bench and confirm VPC/access (by 2/18/26). Lena provide canonical prompts and traces (by 2/16/26). Sales ops will draft SOW (by 2/20/26).
[12:45] Omar: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:50] Lena: thanks, excited to get this moving.
[12:55] Maya: appreciate it, we'll follow up in writing with timeline and links.

--- End transcript ---

Notes on numbers used in call: per-token example pricing are illustrative placeholders. POC deliverables include a dashboard, spreadsheet, A/B quality report, and an executive KPI slide.
